sections.html:
The office is at 205 College Street, Asheville, NC 28801, with weekday service from 8 am until 5 pm. Recording and real estate staff take calls at 828-250-4302, vital records at 828-250-4300 and the help desk at 828-250-4303. Spanish speakers can use 828-250-4307.

A holiday closing calendar is posted on the office's web page, so check it before planning a same-day recording around Thanksgiving or the December holidays. The county website is buncombenc.gov, and older buncombecounty.org links forward there.

Records go back to the 1700s. Anyone who prefers paper can use the public record search room at the same address during office hours.

The office keeps the paper trail for Buncombe land: conveyances, deeds of trust and their cancellations, plats, assumed business names, UCC filings, separation agreements, road maintenance agreements and powers of attorney. All of it is open to public inspection.

Staff act as record keepers. They will not draft or change papers, although forms for satisfactions and assumed names are on hand, and anyone needing a deed drawn up is sent to an attorney. Filings must be originals with live signatures and a notary's acknowledgment.

  • Real estate conveyances and deeds of trust
  • Satisfactions and cancellations after payoff
  • Plats and miscellaneous maps
  • Assumed names and UCC filings
  • Powers of attorney and related papers

Start with paper size, which must be letter or legal. Leave a three-inch blank strip at the top of page one, half an inch on its other edges, and half an inch on every edge of later pages.

  • Black ink, white paper, a legible font of 9 points or bigger.
  • Printing on a single side of each sheet.
  • A title for the instrument written near the top of page one.
  • No highlighter over important information.
  • Color or grayscale images count as non-standard.

Off-standard deeds are accepted at an added $25. A color scan alone triggers it, so have the final deed printed on plain white paper.

Filing fees follow one statewide schedule, while copy rates come from the county.

Typical recording and copy charges at the College Street office
ServiceAmount
Recording a general instrument$26.00 up to page 15, then $4.00 apiece
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 up to page 35, then $4.00 apiece
Cancellation after a loan payoffFree
Off-standard format$25 added on top
Certified copy by mail$5 for the opening page and $2 for each following one
Uncertified copy25 cents a sheet
Excise tax on a deed$1.00 for each $500 of value or part thereof

To order by mail, enclose the Real Estate Records Request Form and a check or money order made out to Register of Deeds. Adding a stamped return envelope speeds things up.

sections.h2: What to bring to College Street
sections.html:
If you are carrying the deed in yourself instead of using a title firm, bring the original with live signatures and the notary's acknowledgment, a check or money order for the recording fee, and the excise tax payment. Count the pages first, because $26.00 covers a general instrument only up to page 15, and a deed of trust covers up to page 35 at $64.00.

Check that the deed is printed on plain white letter or legal paper with the three-inch blank strip on page one. If you want proof of what was recorded, order a certified copy afterward, either at the counter or by mail with the request form. Call 828-250-4302 if you are unsure about any step, though staff cannot give legal advice.

The seller pays the register before the deed is filed. The charge is one dollar on each $500 of price, counting a partial $500 as a whole one.

Buncombe keeps half in its general fund and passes the rest to the state monthly, net of refunds and the county's allowance. Review the excise tax line on the settlement statement, because it follows the price on the deed.

A parcel that straddles two counties pays in the one holding the larger share of its value.

Electronic filing is open to firms. Lenders, law offices, attorneys and surveyors submit through an authorized eRecording provider.

After choosing a provider, the company completes a Submitter Memorandum of Understanding. For a seller this explains how a title firm can have a deed recorded quickly. Individual owners can carry originals to College Street or mail them.

Filed documents can be found in the online records search, which comes with a video tutorial. Results cover deeds, deeds of trust, powers of attorney and assumed names, and can be printed.

On its Real Estate Recording page, the county pairs an Online Records Search with a lookup tutorial. Nearby sit a Parcel Ownership Dashboard, a Cemetery Finder and a Farm Finder. The index runs from conveyances to assumed names, and the oldest entries date to the 1700s.

Use them before listing to verify how title is vested, spot an old easement or catch a deed of trust that was never cleared. If one shows up, contact the lender, who is the one to file the cancellation.

sections.h2: How the 2026 reappraisal delay affects a sale
sections.html:
Buncombe's 2026 tax bills use the 2021 schedule of values because of a state law passed in July 2026, and the new reappraisal takes effect January 1, 2027. The county levy on those bills is 61.54 cents for each $100 of valuation.

The bill due around your closing rests on the older values. You can view bills at tax.buncombenc.gov, and the Tax Assessment office takes questions at 828-250-4920. Our Buncombe property tax guide covers appeals, relief programs and rates.

sections.h2: Renters and investors selling in Buncombe
sections.html: About a third of homes in the county are rented, so some sellers are investors with tenants in place. A lease leaves the register's work unchanged, but your closing attorney should hear about it early so the deed, the tenant's rights and the closing date line up.

sections.h2: Checks before your deed is recorded
sections.html:
Three checks matter: the deed's layout, the excise line and any property tax still owed. Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance has force against lien creditors and buyers only after registration, so recording time sets priority.

An autumn closing can overlap a bill that has been issued but not paid, since bills normally come due September 1 and carry a grace period into early January. Collections answers at 828-250-4910.

Read your own deed in the online search before accepting an offer, including the legal description and easements. If a mortgage was paid off long ago, confirm a satisfaction was recorded, and ask the lender to file one when it was not.

faqs.q: What hours does the Buncombe register keep?
faqs.a: It serves the public weekdays, 8 am to 5 pm, at 205 College Street. Holiday closings follow the county calendar posted on the office's web page.

faqs.q: Will the Buncombe register help draft my deed?
faqs.a: No. Its role is to record and preserve documents, not to write or revise them. Forms for satisfactions and assumed names are available, and deed drafting goes to an attorney.

faqs.q: How much is a certified copy of a Buncombe deed?
faqs.a: Page one of a certified copy is $5 and each later page is $2. Plain copies cost $0.25 a page. Mail orders should enclose payment made out to Register of Deeds.

faqs.q: How much is the Buncombe County deed tax?
faqs.a: The rate is $1.00 on each $500 of price, with any remainder counted as a full $500 unit. The seller settles it before recording, and the county retains half.

faqs.q: What if my Buncombe County deed is not on standard paper?
faqs.a: The deed is recorded, with a $25 non-standard fee on top. Standard means letter or legal paper, black ink, at least 9 point type and the required margins.
